VERIFIED AT FULL RESOLUTION (2026-09-15, native 444x282 and a 2x nearest-neighbour inspection copy). The image is a single screenshot of the Delphi IDE containing, exactly as the host page describes: the main window titled 'Delphi - Project1' with menu bar File / Edit / Search / View / Compile / Run / Options / Tools / Help; a speedbar of two toolbar rows; a tabbed component palette (Standard, Additional, Data Access, Data Controls, Dialogs, System, VBX, Samples); a floating 'Object Inspector' window with an object selector reading 'Warning: TButton', an alphabetical property grid (Cancel, Caption, Cursor, Default, DragCursor, DragMode, Enabled, Font, Height, HelpContext, Hint, Left, ModalResult, Name, ParentFont) and Properties / Events page tabs; a form-design window titled 'Form1' with a dotted alignment grid and a selected TButton captioned 'Warning'; and a code window titled 'UNIT1.PAS' showing Object Pascal source ('type', 'TForm1 = class(TForm)', 'Warning: TButton;', 'procedure WarningClick(Sender: TObject);', 'private', '{ Private declarations }', 'public', '{ Public declarations }') with a status strip reading '28  1  Modified  Insert' and a 'Unit1' page tab.

VERSION MARKERS (Delphi 1, 16-bit): window chrome is Windows 3.x — a minimise/maximise triangle pair at the right of each title bar and a single control-menu box at the left, with no Windows 95 close button, no title-bar 3D bevel and no taskbar. The component palette carries a 'VBX' tab, which is specific to the 16-bit Delphi 1 line (Delphi 2 and later are 32-bit and use OCX/ActiveX rather than VBX). The code editor uses the Delphi 1 filename-titled window ('UNIT1.PAS' in 8.3 uppercase) rather than the later 'Unit1.pas' / project-manager-integrated editor.

NOT PRESENT IN THE IMAGE: no version number string, no About box, no date. The '1.0' identification rests on the vendor URL path and page title plus the 16-bit/VBX/Windows 3.x markers above, not on a number printed in the screenshot.
